name: Robert Hales
role: Prior of the Knights Hospitaller of England; Lord Treasurer
description: Prior of the Order of the Knights Hospitaller (Knights of St John) in England and, from 1380, Lord Treasurer -- the officer directly responsible for administering the poll tax's collection. The Hospitallers' London headquarters at Clerkenwell Priory was singled out and destroyed by the rebels on 13 June specifically because of Hales's office. Found alongside Archbishop Sudbury in the Tower on 14 June 1381 and beheaded with him on Tower Hill without trial; his head, too, was set on London Bridge.
narrative_function: The tax's chief administrator; killed alongside Sudbury as the revolt's second-highest-ranking victim.
